*For the cancelled DLC, see Mars (Downloadable Content).* **Location:** Milky Way / Local Cluster / Sol System /  **Fourth planet** **Prerequisite:** Level 20 (Mass Effect)

Once considered a prospect for terraforming and colonization, the discovery of faster than light travel turned **Mars** into a quiet backwater. Its southern pole is a historical preserve centered on the Prothean ruins found there. Immigration and development are restricted as the search for Prothean artifacts continues.

*See also: Protheans: Martian Ruins* Mars was explored via various robotic expeditions for nearly a century before the first manned research stations were placed in the 2080s. The first permanent settlement on Mars was Lowell City, founded in 2103 by the European Space Agency, and based in Eos Chasma. Within a decade, both the US and China had founded permanent settlements as well. However, satellites near Promethei Planum began reporting strange phenomena that gave the region a 'Bermuda Triangle' reputation, mostly unexplained magnetic field shifts. In 2148, a prospecting team led by Mateus Silva began exploring near the Deseado Crater, and found the source of these disturbances when they unearthed a subterranean Prothean ruin. The ruins contained a malfunctioning mass effect core and several starships, as well as refined element zero. After a global effort, the information remaining in the ruins' computers was translated, identifying the structure as a former observation and biosciences station, set up to receive and process data from Earth as the Protheans studied Cro\-Magnon humans. The motives and conclusions of the Prothean observers remained unknown, but the ruins' data cache, though fragmented, accelerated human sciences by roughly two hundred years. It paved the way for the development of FTL drives and, later, mass effect field technology. Some of the refined element zero in the ruins, however, fell into less responsible hands. Criminal triads on Mars used it to create red sand; the drug may have taken its name from Mars' distinctive colouring and arid surface.
- *Mission:* Priority: Mars
Mars cannot be mined.

- Mars is the only planet in the Sol System whose population does not appear in the planet card when orbited by the Normandy SR\-2. - 2103 also marks the founding of the first permanent Martian colonies in the *Star Trek* universe. |  | **The following information is drawn from cut content and is not to be considered canon in any way.** | | --- | --- |
*Main article: Mars (Downloadable Content)* A cut DLC for Mass Effect would have taken place inside the Prothean ruins on Mars, as well as on the Bonestell Platform orbiting the planet.
The following is a transcription of all texts found within the Mass Effect 2 Art Book published in 2010\. There are no indications on who wrote these commentaries.

The original title in the Mass Effect trilogy set a new standard for emotionally engaging digital actors. To push the quality bar even higher, the art team painstakingly developed sophisticated concepts and new technologies for the characters of Mass Effect 2. Personalities and back stories were woven into every detail of the designs, and several characters were born out of production paintings like this one of the Illusive Man. Capturing more than just his appearance, this painting portrays a moment that defines the spirit of the character. The tank\-bred Grunt was designed to contrast with other krogan by having smoother horns and a showroom\-new armor. After a painful introduction to Shepard, Garrus' appearance for the remainder of the story would bear the scars and bandages of a near\-fatal injury. The Illusive Man’s suit was designed to capture an impeccable futuristic style, combined with the casual swagger of a charming billionaire. Early ideas of Miranda pegged her as a blonde, but once her Cerberus uniform was concepted, black hair seemed to better complement the "femme fatale" look. Jack's extensive tattoos suited her personality better than clothing or armor. The final designs were intricately crafted as a visual story of her past. Samara's armor and jewelry were created with feminine lines and ornate detailing meant to capture her archetypal description of "mystic warrior". Legion presented an opportunity to develop the basic geth design by adding moving parts that allowed it to animate with detailed expressions. Originally added to the concept just for fun, Shepard's N7 armor became an integral part of Legion's appearance and back story. Mordin's design needed to balance the look of a brilliant scientist with that of a combat\-ready tech specialist. Having completed her pilgrimage, Tali's new look was designed to be familiar yet noticeably more mature than in the original story. The design for Thane was one of the most challenging, as he needed to be not only a sleek\-looking alien assassin, but also an attractive potential love interest.

As the scope of the story expanded dramatically in the second part of the trilogy, so did the scale of creatures and enemies faced by the heroes. In particular, the hybridization of humans and Reaper technology is revealed through several stages of increasingly powerful enemies, culminating in the enormous and terrifying Reaper\-human larva shown here in early production paintings. The countless designs for the Reaper\-human larva \[above and previous page] covered a full spectrum between Reaper and human forms. Ultimately, a more human shape was chosen, albeit one that's only partially formed, and of distinctly Reaper construction. Scions are essentially walking genetic experiments, crudely fusing Reaper technology with human anatomy. The Collectors were originally inspired by electron microscope photographs of insect heads. Their full\-body designs ranged from humanoid to highly\-abstract creations. Clearly fusing Collector DNA with the combined brainpower of several human heads, the Praetorians are another example of horrific Reaper experimentation.

Having established a galaxy of locations with the first story, the art team for Mass Effect 2 had the luxury of returning to familiar places to develop them further, or create completely new and exotic locales. This balance helps anchor the story in idyllic and familiar settings like the Citadel (shown here in a matte painting), while offering new locations that reveal the darker side of the Mass Effect universe. Interiors for Cerberus locations \[right] epitomize the clean and geometric design style of the Mass Effect universe, while the concepts for Cerberus' Minuteman Station \[above and opposite] reaffirm its inspiring scope. Because it is an asari homeworld, designs for Ilium \[sic] \[opposite] had to capture the beauty and serenity of the species. While the more elitist locations of the Citadel were featured in the original story, Mass Effect 2 takes players to some of the grittier and more vibrant districts of the enormous space station. \[above] With guards moving through "hamster tubes" to observe the prisoners below, Purgatory's colorless environment \[opposite] offers no hope to its inhabitants. Korlus \[above] is equally grim, fulfilling the promise of the planet's working name: "junk world". The archetypal opposite of the Citadel, Omega is a lawless and dangerous city in space, ruled by powerful gangsters and mercenary groups. Its unique shape was inspired by a blossoming nuclear mushroom cloud. Collector interiors had to feel uncomfortably alien, with vistas of epic proportions. To ground their look in something familiar, artists took inspiration from natural bee hives.

With a fast\-moving story that spans the galaxy, Mass Effect 2 brought new demand for spaceship and vehicle designs. From the rusty krogan hauler shown here to the impressive new incarnation of the starship Normandy, vehicles continue to play a key role in the Mass Effect experience. Perpetually seeking a new homeworld, the ships of the quarian migrant fleet \[sic] \[above] were envisioned as tadpole\-like shapes strapped with myriad cargo containers. To help portray the Collectors as disturbingly insect\-like, the final design for the Collector ship \[opposite, bottom] combines sleek metallic structures with organic shapes inspired by the termite mounds of Australia. With the new Normandy being substantially larger, a shuttle \[right] was designed to transport the squad anywhere the big ship couldn't go. And since it would also be featured in cutscenes and interior shots, its design had to incorporate a detailed interior and functioning doors. For future vehicular missions, the Mako was re\-imagined as a hovering tank \[above]. An enemy of devastating power, the Gunship combines the posture of an attack helicopter with futuristic propulsion and weaponry. With the destruction of the original Normandy \[opposite], the Cerberus\-built Normandy SR2 \[sic] was conceived as a bigger and faster starship, borrowing its sleek proportions from delta\-winged fighter jets. The replacement Normandy was originally meant to feel like a crude knockoff of the original ship: bigger and more powerful, but without the luxuries. The final design, however, featured numerous luxurious improvements, including posh living quarters and a top\-of\-the\-line galley, not to mention wood inlay and leather seats.

With an increased focus on intense tactical combat, Mass Effect 2 brought new opportunities for the team to create weapons with unique designs and spectacular effects. The addition of heavy weapons provided artists the opportunity to create weapons of otherworldly firepower, ranging from the organic but deadly Collector beam weapon \[opposite, bottom] to the ultimate in personal protection, the tactical nuke \[above].

**Mass Effect 2 Character Concepts** is an internal document which contains concepts from the development team for the squadmates of Mass Effect 2. The following is a partial transcription of this document, according to what has been shown by writer Mac Walters. A number of these concepts were further refined or merged into final squadmates, while other ideas were dropped entirely. In addition, this page also contains a retranscription of the beginning of another document called "Acquisition \& Loyalty Missions". Note that parts of these documents are missing; this transcription was made on the basis of the segments shown in the video linked in references.

Female human, 35 **Enabling Mission** Ordered to help the player by Cerberus' head — the enigmatic Illusive Man. She is his protégé, and her loyalty can be secured by helping her learn more about him. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** The product of extensive genetic engineering by a wealthy couple, she enjoys intelligence, reflexes, strength, and beauty superior to other humans. As the literal "best daughter money can buy," she is aristocratic and superior. She gets what she wants, and right now she wants Shepard.

Male human, 30 **Enabling Mission** Assigned by Cerberus to help the player. Years ago, he was involved with Superwoman. She's over it, he's not — secure his loyalty by helping him forget her, or getting them back together. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Taciturn and resolute, a good\-hearted man with strong personal morals. He is soft\-spoken and polite, almost "southron" in his manners. A veteran soldier, he is the classic "big brother" platoon sergeant — basically Corporal Hicks from *Aliens*.

Geth, ageless and gender\-neutral **Enabling Mission** The player recovers the memory core of a damaged geth "boss" creature, opening a collection quest. As the player clears UCW geth bases, he collects parts to rebuild it. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Geth form a networked intelligence. This individual is sophisticated enough to be intelligent without a network, but it still faces a terrifying silence in its mind. To cope, it partitions its personality into three unique personalities.

Male Prothean\-tech hologram, partially disabled, memory banks failing, set adrift in space. **Enabling Mission** During one of the Space Combat sections, we meet an "energy being": a floating version of the Prothean hologram who. \[sic] He has become detached from his docking unit; this scrambled his memory circuits, disrupted his physical form, and began a slow and inevitable process of decay. The Hologram's only hope is to find an operational docking unit so that he can stabilize himself. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Back when the Protheans were still around, the holograms were in the middle of a civil rights movement to be treated as equals. He's still touchy about being referred to as anything less than a sentient equal, and it can provide for humor in some really odd situations. Could eventually be restored into the true appearance and form of a Prothean.

Male krogan, 0 **Enabling Mission** Cerberus gives the player a krogan breeding chamber. With a little genetic material from a suitable "parent" (Wrex is a good choice if he's not dead), the player gets an adult krogan to raise as Paragon or Renegade. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He's a massive killing machine with the intellectual and moral development of a child. His lack of social etiquette often has him saying the wrong thing and the wrong time. \[sic]

A deactivated 75 year old robot. **Enabling Mission** Shepard will have to buy the Tank. This will make money in the game interesting and encourage scavenging (more exploration). The Player will also have to scavenge or buy a large enough power cell for the robot to function. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** It's a big robot. Who doesn't love that? Plus, the robot could have illegal AI which would make traveling back to Citadel space interesting (you're harboring an illegal AI). We could also get into interesting themes of slavery \- you do own the robot.

Femake krogan, (human equivalent \- 30 years old) **Enabling Mission** She's a high ranking member of the Krogan Breeders guild who's comes \[sic] to the Citadel *\[?]* against Shepard and for answers about the choice to destroy the cure to the Genophage. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** *\[?]* to the player in a seemingly humorous *\[?]* in Wrex. Her agenda is to find a cure *\[?]* all female Krogan's under Reaper control to send back to the krogan home world for breeding *\[?]* testing. This character will allow us to expand on the desperate state of the krogan species and further explore their culture as it exists under threat of extinction.

Male salarian, 11 (human equivalent: 28\) **Enabling Mission** He's hunted by Kirrahe's squad (either led by Kirrahe or by his second in command) for the murder of a salarian politician. That politician held secret information that the player needs, and the Avenger now has. The player must convince Kirrahe's team that keeping him alive is more beneficial. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He has spent his entire life training to become the perfect assassin, to the abandonment of friends, family and other personal connections. A descendent \[sic] of the League of One, he wants nothing more than revenge for their eradication.

Quarian, female, 22ish **Enabling Mission** Tali would be an in with the Quarians \[sic] for the jump drive. Her missions could involve restoring her reputation with her people. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Tali is one of the few who believes in Shepard throughout his whole ordeal. She has finished her pilgrimage, but her belief in Shepard and the reapers \[sic] has made her a bit of a pariah with many of her people. She admits her infatuation with Shepard, saying that she never pursued it in ME 1 due to the presence of Ashley or Liara (or Kaidan if Tali swings both ways). Many players would have immediate buy in with her character since she is familiar from ME 1\. *(Missing segment)* *(Missing)* Shepard's past? How did she end up a pirate queen, roaming the fringes of space and separated from the Migrant Fleet?

Male quarian, 25 **Enabling Mission** He's in the middle of a gun battle between police and bounty hunters; they're all after him. He was seeking information to prove that it's safe to return to the quarian homeworld now that the geth are less of a threat, but his curiosity and impish behavior left him with a bounty on his head a warrant for his arrest **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Roguish and charming, he's is constantly getting himself in and out of trouble, concocting crazy schemes that never quite work out as planned. His tech abilities, like many of his kind, are extraordinary.

Any race, male or female, 30ish years old. **Enabling Mission** After hearing rumors of Shepard's mission, he approaches saying he has needed contact information. He leads the player through the dark underbelly of black market society. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** This charismatic rascal has all the connections. He loves all people, seeing the good side even in the bad guys, and as such has friends and contacts in all organizations. He'll follow a paragon or renegade Shepard equally with a smile. He's got the free spirit of Han Solo with naïve enthusiasm of Luke Skywalker. He would be a good source of humor since he'll be jovial in the worst of situations and could play off more rugged Wrex\-type characters.

Male or female Quarian \[sic] Mid\-30s or 40s. **Enabling Mission** When you meet up with the Quarians (perhaps on the floatilla), \[sic] this character seeks you out and wants to join you. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Basically the idea comes from the crazy Irishman in *Braveheart*. Geth killed thousands of Quarians, \[sic] including dozens of this character's friends, relatives, and fellow soldiers (if he/she's a soldier). This character wants revenge but is very "whimsical" about it, like the Irishman. "Do I get to kill Geth?" \[sic] "Yes, you get to kill Geth." \[sic] "Excellent!"

Female human, 25 **Enabling Mission** She and the player are trying to steal the same thing. The player wins, but it becomes clear that she let the player "win"... this time. Alternately, she could try to steal the LEVIATHAN. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** She's not just a common thief, she specializes in stealing ships. Big ones, small ones; it's doesn't matter. Her skills and success make her confident, and she's chatty and positive. She's small enough to get in to and out of almost any tight spot, and when her body fails her, her brilliant hacking skills take over.

Female human, 25 years old **Enabling Mission** She operates in the Terminus system \[sic] going where no else can. In exchange for Shepard's help in completing a mission, she will help him in the assault on PLANET FORTRESS. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** She's a highly skilled thief who can get jobs done that no one else can. She's the best of the best and would prove a valuable asset to Shepard.

Female asari, 400 (human equivalent: 30\) **Enabling Mission** The player does not know she is a Spectre; she was sent by the Council to investigate the "imposter" claiming to be Shepard. She ambushes Shepard on Omega, and the player *(Missing)* *(Missing segment)*

Male batarian, 27 **Enabling Mission** The player learns the location of an infamous batarian terrorist — an expert in technology, hacking, etc. When they find him they discover he isn't actually a terrorist, and bears no ill will towards humanity. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He's basically a nerd — meek, socially awkward and uncomfortable in combat and confrontation. He is, however, incredible with his tech skills. He wants to live a quiet, ordinary life, but is so brilliant he will never be seen as normal or ordinary.

Male salarian; (Human or Quarian could work too); 36 **Enabling Mission** The player needs to track down the leader of a rebel movement known for infiltrating impregnable enemy territory with ease. His rebellion was crushed, and since then he has been living off\-the\-grid, successfully evading dozens of attempts to capture or kill him. The player must race against vicious bounty hunters as they follow a trail of underground contacts scattered across several star systems. **Why is he cool, amusing or interesting?** He's an extraordinary guerrilla fighter, resourceful and adaptable, able to hack systems and rig technology with MacGyver\-like ease. He controls a shadowy network of contacts, giving him access to important information and exotic technologies. He's still passionate about his cause, was personally involved in the tragic injustice that sparked his rebellion, and gives the player an opportunity to finish his fight. His grand cause should be something where a bunch of oppressed underdogs take on a powerful government or corporation. For example, he may have united several warring colonies in an attempt to shut down the arms company that had triggered the war and was supplying all sides.

Male human, 30 **Enabling Mission** He's been in the Terminus Systems for years, selling his expertise to the highest bidder. Cerberus suggests him as a local guide. If the player doesn't keep his loyalty up he will sell the player out to the COLLECTORS for a nice profit. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He's the gruff, tattooed soldier\-of\-fortune who's seen and done it all. He has hundreds of war stories and carries enough firepower to take out a city block. He's gruff, crude, and says what he thinks, consequences be damned.

Male NEW ALIEN, 35 **Enabling Mission** The player negotiates to obtain a siege weapon built by the NEW ALIENS, which is needed to break into PLANET FORTRESS. They will provide one so long as the player accepts an observer who will ensure the weapon is used only for moral purposes. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** An alien religious or "Teutonic Knight," allowing an element of Firefly's Shepherd Book; a spiritual man living among heathens. He is moody, cynical, and prefers solitude, but possesses unmistakable intelligence and a passionate nature. He must be presented as darkly charismatic and sexually charged despite his "Mr. Rochester" exterior — a strong man that romantic souls want to learn more about.

Any race, male or female, 40ish years old **Enabling Mission** Shepard needs a medical expert and hears about a genius doctor who inexplicably left his position at a top\-secret genetics lab. Shepard tracks down the doctor to find him drinking himself to death in a forgotten hive of scum and villainy. The missions would involve getting the paragon past the issues he is having by righting the wrong or reaping revenge. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He's a doctor who once believed in the cause, but life has beaten him down so that he now questions the good of humanity. Shepard can either foster his hope and bring him back to the light, or push him deeper down his new found renegade path.

Any race, male or female, 20ish. **Enabling Mission** Shepard needs a demolitions expert, and he hears the stories of a demolition\-savant who's just crazy enough to join in on a suicidal mission. The demolitionist needs the state of the art technology to do the job right, so Shepard needs to break into high security black ops bases. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He's a guy who is obviously a bit off, bordering on suicidal crazy. He could be a good source of humor, or a good character study as in Mel Gibson in the original Lethal Weapon.

Male, human, 30 years old **Enabling Mission** The player needs the help of the most dangerous, deadly killer in the galaxy... but first they have to bust him out of the Terminus Systems' most impregnable high\-security prison. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** *(Missing)*

male salarian, 45 **Enabling Mission** Shepard becomes embroiled in race against government agents to track down an anarchist hacker living on an isolationist commune inhabited by the space age equivalent of pot\-heads and flower children. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** The classic stoner (think Tommy Chong), but he is a brilliant techno\-geek. Carefree and easy\-going to the point he can barely even remember to buy himself groceries, he is also able to hack into and reprogram highly complicated encrypted networks.

male salarian, \[sic] 30 **Enabling Mission** On Omega, the player learns about a vigilante turian bounty hunter who is trying to bring down one of the criminal gangs. It turns out to be Garrus, finishing off the accomplices of Dr. Saleaon \[sic] (his party member plot in ME1\). **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Players will see how the familiar Garrus has grown and changed, and many players might enjoy having him on their side again. Plus, he's a bounty hunter, capturing wanted criminals who try to run to escape the law. *(Possible missing segment)*

**Character Hook** She was the product of extensive genetic engineering by a wealthy couple, and enjoys strength, reflexes, intelligence, and beauty superior to other humans. At the start of the game she is assigned to help Shepard. She's a young woman (35\). At some point in the past, she took CERBERUS MALE as a lover. She's over it, he isn't. Her genetic advantages and intense personality helped her rise quickly in Cerberus. She is a protégé of ILLUSIVE MAN, who is grooming her to replace him. She's conscious of this. She wants the job, but she also knows that she'll be dropped if she fails to perform. **Character Details** A manipulative predator. She is cool, haughty, and aristocratic. When she finds a man interesting, she will lure him in with a raised brow and a small smile. She seduces him with her personality and sensuality, makes a plaything of him, and moves on when bored. She's taken many lovers, but ultimately loves only herself. People only have use to her so long as they are interesting. Her tendency to treat people as toys is an extension of her upbringing. As the literal "best daughter money could buy," she was treated as a useful investment or vanity trophy. **Story Role** She serves as an intelligence analyst in Cerberus. You need to know where someone is? She can find out. You need to acquire a fusion bomb? She knows people. **Relationship** Throughout the game she is searching for files with information about ILLUSIVE MAN. If you help her, you find conflicting urban legends. She pursues male Shepard aggressively. If you're willing, she will take him to bed very quickly, but (if her loyalty is low) get bored with him just as fast. She is also toying with CERBERUS MALE on the side. If her loyalty is continues \[sic] to grow (as ascending series of checks), she will confide more in Shepard. It is possible to open her heart. While still driven to succeed ILLUSIVE MAN (her career is more important to her than any lover), she will be easier on the crew, and less likely to treat partners (including poor CERBERUS MALE) as disposable.

**Character Hook** CERBERUS MALE is a seasoned Alliance soldier who served on the frontier for nearly a decade . \[sic] He was at Eden Prime, where he fought a geth ambusher hand\-to\-hand... and won. Few in his unit did. Since then, he's avoided VIs and cybernetics. Cerberus was impressed by his performance (and his new conviction that humanity is too vulnerable). He worked with CERBERUS FEMALE for some time, the brawn to her brains. She took him as one of her many lovers. He felt that they had bonded, but she saw him as fun hunk of man\-meat. She fooled around on the side, and after they were reassigned forgot him entirely. He still has a picture of her up in his quarters. He is 28 — younger than Shepard. **Character Details** Taciturn and resolute, a good\-hearted man with strong personal morals. He is soft\-spoken and polite, almost "southron" in his manners. He keeps his emotions to himself. He watches over the crew of LEVIATHAN with a light touch, but near\-omniscience. Little occurs without his knowledge. Wlien it comes to the safety of the crew, it goes from God, to Shepard, to him. The crew affectionately call him "Old Man." **Story Role** At the start of the game, he's your primary fire support, a role similar to Ashley's. **Relationship** He's concerned that he may have done wrong in previous missions alongside CERBERUS FEMALE — that he was blinded by his devotion to her. He will talk about some of the things they did together. If his loyalty to Shepard grows stronger than his loyalty to Cerberus, the player can tell him whether to stay or go. Working alongside CERBERUS FEMALE again has rekindled the old spark. CERBERUS FEMALE begins seducing him again. Shepard can intervene, or let her have her way. She will eventually tire and leave him — possibly preferring her relationship with Shepard. If the player doesn't intervene, and has not persuaded CERBERUS FEMALE to care more about others, CERBERUS MALE will attempt suicide in his quarters. If his loyalty is high and the player has good persuades, he can be talked off the ledge. *(Possible missing segment)*

**Character Hook** Much like Inigo Montoya in the Princess Bride (You killed my father, prepare to die!), SALARIAN is obsessed with avenging those responsible for the deaths of his revered ancestors. **Character Details** A descendent \[sic] of the League of One, he wants nothing more than revenge for their eradication. Driven by his obsession, he has spent his entire life training to become the perfect assassin, to the abandonment of friends, family and other personal connections. His single\-mindedness often reveals itself in odd ways (i.e. commenting on things relevant to his search, but which seem completely unrelated to the situation at hand). **Story Role** When Shepard finds SALARIAN, he's being hunted by Kirrahe's former squad (either led by Kirrahe or by his second in command). He/She is wanted for the murder of a high ranking salarian politician. It turns out, that politician held secret information (about PLANET FORTRESS??) that the player needs. After reaching SALARIAN, the player must convince Kirrahe's team that keeping SALARIAN alive is more beneficial (stand down), or they must be defeated. Either way, SALARIAN agrees to come with you after you save his/her life, and turns over the information he took from the politician. **Relationship** A great person to have around when you need a sniper; SALARIAN is one of the best in the galaxy, as long as you can keep him. SALARIAN will follow the player willingly for a time, hoping to uncover clues in places he has yet to search. However, if the player cannot get SALARIAN's loyalty high enough, there may come a time when he chooses his path over Shepard's (a chance to kill one of his prey that can't be missed). It doesn't need to end in them leaving the party, but it could cause the player some "difficulties" on a mission.

**Character Hook** He's Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid; rolled together in to \[sic] one boisterous, but highly capable quarian infiltrator. **Character Details** Roguish and charming QUARIAN is constantly getting himself in and out of trouble, often concocting crazy schemes that never quite work out as planned. His tech abilities, like many of his kind, are extraordinary, but he's also great in a fight. Though his "way with words" often seems a bit strange, it usually comes off as endearing (especially to his friends). He enjoys a good fight and he often finds one, despite protestations that he was innocent of any wrong doing. **Story Role** When the player finds QUARIAN he's on OMEGA in the middle of a gun battle between the local authorities and mercenary bounty hunters; and they're all after him. Despite seeming like he's a bit vulnerable, he handles himself well and dispatches several of the bounty\-hunters on his own before being rescued by the player. QUARIAN came to OMEGA seeking answers regarding the geth, hoping to prove to his people that it's safe to return to their original home planet now that the geth are much less of a threat. But his curiosity and impish behavior left him with a bounty on his head a warrant for his arrest. \[sic] **Relationship** Romance interest for the straight female PC. At first his advances on the player are typical flirts that he might have with any female. But when the player reciprocates it piques his interest. He admits he's intrigued by the player, but wonders if the player is only interested in him because he's different. As long as the player doesn't go totally renegade, the romance remains viable. If the player crosses the line too many times, he'll call it off.

**Character Hook** A ship\-stealing rogue, she's the typical thief with the heart of gold. Cute and friendly, YOUNG THIEF has an uncanny knack for never getting caught. She'll steal your heart, and then your ship! **Character Description** YOUNG THIEF is the quintessential thief/hacker. She doesn't see anything wrong with stealing from the rich. Her skills and success give her a confidence, and she's very chatty. Generally positive in her outlook, she isn't afraid to speak her mind... though sometimes she can be a bit naïve, seeing complex moral situations in simple "good" and "evil" lights. Lithe and small, she can get in to and out of almost any tight spot. And when her body fails her, her brilliant "hacking" skills take over. Though she's beholden to know one, she respects the player immediately and follows out of loyalty and curiosity. **Story Role** When the player meets YOUNG THIEF they are trying to steal the same thing. The player eventually wins, but it becomes clear that she let the player "win"... this time. She's decent with a pistol, but needs a bit of protection in a fight. She's not just any thief, she specializes in stealing ships. Big ones, small ones; it doesn't matter. She usually works alone, but the player has piqued her curiosity and she's willing to come along for the ride... for the time being. **Relationship** Romance for lesbian female PC. She's not looking for another "relationship". But now she finds herself strangely attracted to the female player (she's platonically curious about the male player, but keeps her distance due to her current distrust/dislike of men). For her, this isn't a "relationship"... it's a fling. It's exciting. It's new. It's different. She doesn't care if it ends today, or goes on for a long time. As the story progresses, she begins to get antsy. She's used to working alone. If the player hasn't brought her loyalty up enough, she will leave.

**Character Hook** Since this character will be used to introduce a new alien race, his background, critical path role, and character arc cannot be decided until more details on that race are available. Tali without the Pilgrimage and Wrex without his father's armor wouldn't have been as interesting. There has been discussion of making him an emissary of an alien religion or "Teutonic Knight," allowing an element of Firefly's Shepherd Book; a spiritual man living among heathens. **Character Details** He is moody, cynical, and prefers solitude, but possesses unmistakable intelligence and a passionate nature. He must be presented as darkly charismatic and sexually charged despite his cold, hostile exterior — a strong man that romantic souls want to learn more about. He can be angered, but tends to smolder silently. When he finally breaks, it's with "consequences be damned" bluntness. Unlike Wrex, he is literate and erudite — more likely to make a cutting remark than punch you in the face. **Story Role** TBD
Owner(s) Draft Signoff Review Signoff Production Signoff

Garrus — a tough war veteran, still trying to do the right the thing, but in his own way. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Garrus returns, but he's the de facto leader of a small group of elite vigilantes. His team is under no banner, beholden to no one. No longer the eager protégé, he has become a hard, experienced warrior thanks to everything Shepard taught him. He has the battle scars and war stories to prove it. **Background** Since Shepard's "death", Garrus became increasingly disillusioned with the Council's bureaucratic crap. He's slowly gathered a small group (6 or less) of elite "soldiers" willing to do whatever it takes to put an end to tyranny. The tyrants of the universe have been put on notice. Unfortunately, in the Council's eyes, the only people with authority to act in this way are the Spectres. At the moment, Garrus is having some troubles of his own. The last few missions have gone poorly... as though someone was being tipped off to his team's arrival. Garrus decided to put his team on hiatus for a short time while he investigated further. During his absence, things have gone horribly wrong back at his main base of operations. **Narrative Razor (Acquisition)** Omega: While away investigating, Garrus leams that his base has been infiltrated and the last of his men are being held hostage. He's sure it's a trap to catch him (his men are probably already dead), but he's got to go anyway, he won't let them die in vain. When the player arrives on the scene, it's dead body after dead body. There's still several "enemies" (the mole has tipped off several of the factions that Garrus' group have helped cripple — they've teamed up to get payback). Eventually, the player gets close to Garrus. He's holed up in a defensive position, picking off his attackers. Now the attackers are between you and Garrus, but they're making a push. Garrus' time is running out. When the player finally reaches Garrus, he's been badly wounded and must be taken back to the Normandy to get patched up. **Narrative Razor (Loyalty)** Citadel: Garrus reveals that he's learned about the mole in his organization. He needs to finish this guy off. The mole is working for a group of near\-do\-wells that want revenge against Garrus and his team (the mole essentially turned Judas). The player must first hunt down the heads of this cartel (in a meeting on the citadel) and then discover the location of the mole. Once the player has eliminated the cartel members, Garrus sends a message using their computer to the mole, to set up a meeting. The meeting is in a public place and Garrus heads off to find a place from which to snipe him. The Player can persuade Garrus that violence isn't necessary; Shepard can get a confession out of him. Or, player can just let Garrus go on his merry sniping way. Even if the player persuades Garrus to calm down, he says he's taking his gun, just in case. You have the meeting while Garrus is "setting up" in the rafters somewhere. If the player fails to persuade the MOLE, Garrus takes the shot.
*(Missing)*

ASSASSIN is one of the most notorious hitmen in the galaxy. Now he's dying and wants to atone for his sins. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** He combines elements of the deadly stealth killer with a crusader like drive to make up for past mistakes. He's trying to atone for his past sins, but years of training and instincts make the old habits hard to kill. Romance character for female Shepard. **Background** ASSASSIN became a deadly hitman at a relatively young age. He didn't do it out of anger or revenge; it was just a job (Martin in Grosse Point Blank), \[sic] At one he tried to start a family, but he kept the two worlds completely separate. Unfortunately, his past caught up with him and his wife was assassinated. ASSASSIN decided then to break off all contact with his children and other family members. He focused everything on his work and become one of the most notorious assassins in the galaxy. Then, a few years ago, ASSASSIN learned he was dying. Though his job remains the same, he has changed his approach. He no longer takes jobs indiscriminately, but chooses ones that seem to be on the side of "right" (i.e. wiping out a corrupt official). He's also become someone notorious for dealing harshly with anyone who tries to screw him over. But none of this seems to be helping ease the burden of a life of murder; until the player comes along and offers him a shot a \[sic] true redemption. **Narrative Razor (Acquisition)** Asari World: ASSASSIN is on a mission to take down a corrupt official located in an IMPENATRABLE FORTRESS. Your contact suggests if you want a meeting, find him at the hit (after that... you may never see him again). The hit will probably be the Asari \[sic] from ME1 who had you wipe out her sister, the smuggler. The player must infiltrate the IMPENATRABLE FORTRESS head on. After slaughtering their way through dozens of elite guards, the player finds the target of the hit. Just when they're about to begin a discussion, ASSASSIN arrives and finishes her off. He tips his hat and thanks the player for creating such a great distraction, "I knew I could count on you". He gave away his location to the contact hoping to get the player to aid him unknowingly. **Narrative Razor (Loyalty)** Citadel: Assassin left his family (children) to go on his crusade. He hasn't seen them in almost 5 years (and even then, he didn't "make contact"). He's recently learned that his son, now almost 20 years old, has learned not only about some of ASSASSIN's past, but about his mother's death. He's taken it upon himself to become an assassin like his father, but not as a job, for revenge. ASSASSIN doesn't want to see his son make the same mistakes he did. ASSASSIN wants you to help him stop his son from "getting revenge". It may mean killing the target before the son can, or convincing him to turn his life around. Either way, there should be a confrontation between father and son.

All text was copied accurately, and any typos or errors are verbatim. **Context:** Reaper IFF: it was confirmed by writer Chris L'Etoile that these voicelines belonged to Dr. Chandana, before he would show up as a husk boss at the end of the level. **Speaker**: - Chandana --- **Chandana**: It was lonely. It called to us. It wanted to remember. The Masters had been gone so long. The Masters were lost when it was shattered. Currents swept through their inner worlds. They were turned to noise. Babble. The worlds were empty. But the body lived. It lay fallow. The heart pumped. The lungs breathed. But the mind forgot the Masters. It called and They did not answer. We have become an echo of Their echo. We have become more than we were. Join us. Know us. Remember all our lives. We are no longer afraid. You would never be lonely again. We are not your enemy. We only wish to share ourselves. We can join them. We can be like them. We can reach the end of evolution. Do not fear. It is wonderful to be us. We understand ourselves. You cannot defeat them. They will lead us into eternity. If you could only see how we see. Know what we've learned. They were called imshai. Those who lived here before. Reaper. One. A mechanical device used to cut ripened grain. Two. One who gathers a harvest. Harvest. One. The consequence of an event or series of events. Two. The yield of a growing season. Three. To gather. Shepard. They know you. They wish you to understand. They are shepherds, too.

|  | **The following information is drawn from cut content and is not to be considered canon in any way.** | | --- | --- | A variety of content made for Mass Effect 2 was not implemented in the game's final version, or is inaccessible for any reason. In comparison to Mass Effect and Mass Effect 3, known cut content for this game is not as expansive. A large part of it covers inaccessible reactions from squadmates during missions taking place before they can be recruited, due to a late\-development change in the availability of recruitment missions. Some amount of information however was found in relation to Kasumi and Zaeed's recruitment and loyalty missions' earlier development stages, as well as for some of the game's downloadable content. **Note:**  this page only contains brief summaries of a page's related cut content. Click on the link to each individual page to access its more detailed Cut Content section. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

- Prologue: Awakening – there are alternate dialogues for Wilson, Jacob and Shepard. - Freedom's Progress – the vorcha would have first appeared in this mission, and the Illusive Man's debriefing contains several unused alternate voicelines. - Horizon – the player would control colonist Lilith during the Collector attack. Tali has available reactions throughout the mission, even though she cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. - Collector Ship – Legion has available reactions throughout the mission, even though he cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. There are also a few alternate voicelines during the Illusive Man's debriefing. - Reaper IFF – a boss fight with indoctrinated Dr. Chandana and the option to leave Legion on the Reaper were cut. - Collector Base: The Long Walk – Mordin could volunteer as a biotic specialist. - Collector Base: The Final Battle – EDI, Harbinger and Shepard's squadmates have several unused voicelines.

- Dossier: Archangel – unused squadmate reactions exist for squadmates who cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. - Dossier: Tali – there are references to Geth Hoppers being in this level, and an additional demolition charge to pick up. - Dossier: The Assassin – a few squadmate reactions and a Renegade interrupt during Thane's prayer were removed. - Dossier: The Convict – unused squadmate reactions exist for squadmates who cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. - Dossier: The Justicar – squadmates have unused voicelines, including asking Shepard to take a biotic squadmate along in order to take advantage of Minagen X3's effects. - Dossier: The Master Thief – data indicates Kasumi Goto would have been recruited on Illium instead of the Citadel, in a mission where Shepard would battle a pursuing gunship on the rooftops. - Dossier: The Professor – unused squadmate reactions exist for squadmates who cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. - Dossier: The Veteran – at one point, Zaeed Massani was planned to have an actual recruitment mission which would have taken place on Korlus and involved dealing with organized crime, and even had a Mako driving section. - Dossier: The Warlord – unused squadmate reactions exist for squadmates who cannot be recruited yet at this point in the game. An option to execute the wounded mercenary at the start was also removed.

- Grunt: Rite of Passage – in the aftermath, Grunt could have disapproved of Shepard making the decision not to join Uvenk's clan on his behalf. - Jack: Subject Zero – the Collectors would have been present. - Jacob: The Gift of Greatness – a different narrative involved primitive aliens worshipping the crash survivors. - Kasumi: Stealing Memory – data references an alternative version of Kasumi Goto's loyalty mission called "Kasumi: Memento or Mori", in which she and Shepard would try to foil a corporate plot. Additionally, the mission with Donovan Hock had different dialogues. - Miranda: The Prodigal – unused data implies Niket could be saved, and the Illium police had a significant role in the mission. - Tali: Treason – unused journal entries point to additional objectives in this mission, and Legion could testify during the trial. Also, it was possible to somehow miss Rael'Zorah's body on the Alarei. - Thane: Sins of the Father – the person being interrogated could end up dead. - Zaeed: The Price of Revenge – an alternative version of this mission called "Zaeed: Headliner" taking place on Tuchanka required to deal with another bounty hunter, faking Zaeed's death in the process. There are also a number of cut voicelines for the mission on Zorya.

- Citadel: Crime in Progress – it was possible at one point to talk to the salarian game salesman for this quest. - Illium: Blue Rose of Illium – Ereba has a few unused ambient lines. - Illium: Conrad Verner – Conrad has different lines which were supposed to play if he was charmed in the first game. - Illium: Indentured Service – the slave broker would have been batarian instead of asari. - N7: Archeological Dig Site – interacting with the Prothean console would trigger a different scene. - Omega: The Patriarch – Patriarch's assassins have a few unused voicelines.

- Citadel: Mysterious Stranger – cut assignment about a romantic relationship between an asari dancer and a Terra Firma activist. - Illium: Drunk Asari – cut assignment about preventing an Eclipse mercenary from recruiting a drunk asari. - Omega: Beggar Bowl – cut assignment in which Marsh tasks Shepard with dealing with some beggars. - Tuchanka: Female Quest – cut assignment about an investigation into the murder of an Urdnot female.

- Normandy Crash Site – instead of static shots, the development script appears to reference flashbacks in the form of video montages. - Project Firewalker: Prothean Site – unused log fragments would have clearly established that Dr. Cayce is Manuel from the first game. - Overlord – a new type of fish could be acquired here, the camel fish. - Overlord: Prometheus Station – a few Cerberus worker logs were left unused. - Lair of the Shadow Broker – there are several cut voicelines throughout the mission and its aftermath. - Arrival – several voicelines were cut throughout the mission. It was also possible to free other prisoners on Aratoht.

- The M35 Mako was planned to be in the game early in development. - A confrontation between Mordin and Grunt could occur after their loyalty missions were completed, similar to the ones between Miranda and Jack or between Tali and Legion. - In Shepard's first visit to the Citadel, it was possible at one point to go to talk to David Anderson before going down to the Wards, which would have resulted in different interactions with Haron. - A pet robot named "Sparky" is mentioned as a purchasable item in unused text strings. In Mass Effect 3, a similar robot appears as KEI\-9. - Evidence points to a M\-44 Hammerhead training simulation having been planned. - The Presidium Groundskeeper had many ambient lines which cannot be heard in the final game. - On the Normandy, some of EDI's room descriptions to Shepard would have been fully cinematic. - Preitor Gavorn on Omega has a cut greeting dialogue with Shepard. - Codex entries: several entries were cut from the game, though most are present on the N7 HQ website: - Aliens: Non\-Council Races: Reapers: Computers *(missing)* - Aliens: Non\-Council Races: Reapers: Construction *(missing)* - Aliens: Non\-Sapient Creatures: Collectors: Oculi - Aliens: Non\-Council Races: Drell - Humanity and the Systems Alliance: Systems Alliance - Humanity and the Systems Alliance: Systems Alliance: Military Ranks - Organizations: Eldfell\-Ashland Energy - Ships and Vehicles: Sovereign *(different from "Aliens: Non\-Council Races: Sovereign" found in\-game)* - Technology: Communications: Quantum Entanglement Communicators (QEC) - Technology: Computers: Synthetics - Weapons, Armor and Equipment: Enforcement Gauntlets - Weapons, Armor and Equipment: M\-100 Grenade Launcher - Weapons, Armor and Equipment: Omni\-gel - Weapons, Armor and Equipment: Thermal Clips - Several emails from the Illusive Man and Kirrahe were made inaccessible. - A large part of the Shadow Broker's dossier for Samara was left unused, and a few videos in the archive were also cut. - The player could help Morinth feed, notably by finding victims on the Citadel, or sending Kelly Chambers to her. - Several star clusters were cut, including the Perseus Veil and Annos Basin (as Annos Sanctuary), as well as Susskind Station. - An accomplishment related to biotics was unused. - Evidence for different upgrades for squadmates was uncovered. - Another harvestible resource called "Turbonium" was planned at one point. - Many news bulletins were left unheard in the final game, though several were restored in the Legendary Edition.

*For a summary of when various NPC allies become available to join Shepard's crew and an overview of their capabilities, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 2\).* Prologue missions take place at the beginning of the game, in mandatory progression. At the end of the prologue Shepard receives command of the Normandy SR\-2 and is free to explore both the ship and the galaxy. Prologue: Save Joker \- *Story and setting* Prologue: Awakening \- *Create your Shepard, Tutorial* Freedom's Progress \- *First mission with Miranda and Jacob* Stop the Collectors \- *Master mission for the rest of the game*

Act 1 begins when Shepard receives the Stop the Collectors master mission along with command of the Normandy SR\-2 and continues until the mission to Horizon, which is activated as soon as Shepard has recruited all four of Mordin, Garrus, Jack, and Grunt. Any other missions and assignments not completed during Act 1 can still be completed during Act 2\. Note that the order in which squadmates are recruited during Act 1 is entirely up to Shepard and will not affect how events play out in any way. You will also have the opportunity to perform various assignments—some are available on Omega, some on the Citadel, and others you can discover during the process of Planet Scanning. Assignments described as N7 Assignments usually involve squad deployments and combat—effectively small missions—and provide experience, credits, and other rewards. All assignments are optional, but they help advance the story and provide the opportunity for additional rewards and items.

Perform dossier missions to recruit new squad members for your team. It is recommended that you recruit Mordin first so that you will be able to take advantage of upgrades in the Research Lab on the Normandy. When these four missions have all been completed, the Horizon mission will trigger and Act 2 will begin. Dossier: The Professor \- Mordin Dossier: Archangel \- Garrus Dossier: The Convict \- Jack Dossier: The Warlord \- Grunt

The following DLC missions and assignments can be performed during Act 1, or saved until Act 2 if desired. Dossier: The Veteran \- Zaeed Dossier: The Master Thief \- Kasumi Zaeed: The Price of Revenge \- Loyalty Kasumi: Stealing Memory \- Loyalty Overlord Firewalker Pack Normandy Crash Site
When all four of the original (non\-DLC) dossier missions are complete, the Horizon mission will be activated and Act 2 will begin. Horizon

Act 2 begins upon successful completion of the Horizon mission. At this point the Normandy is able to travel to Illium and new dossiers and missions become available. New assignments also become available during the course of Act 2: some at Illium, some on Tuchanka, and many new N7 Assignments open up through Planet Scanning in new systems which open up for exploration. New merchants also become available, along with new items at some of the Act 1 merchants; see the Merchants Guide for a complete list of locations and wares.

Four more squadmates can now be recruited, though Legion's mission works differently in that it does not become available until after the Collector Ship mission, and triggers additional act progression. You will need at least eight total crew members, not counting Legion, to advance the plot. Dossier: The Assassin \- Thane Dossier: The Justicar \- Samara Dossier: Tali \- Tali Reaper IFF \- Legion

Starting in Act 2, speaking with squad members on the Normandy will elicit requests for you to perform Loyalty missions. Securing the loyalty of your squad will both unlock new powers for them and increase the likelihood that they, and indeed Shepard, will survive Act 3\. All loyalty missions are optional—they increase the power of your team but are not required to be completed for the game to progress. Miranda's and Jacob's missions can be obtained immediately when Act 2 begins. Additional missions become available one at a time in the order listed; if the character whose loyalty mission would normally unlock is not yet present (e.g. Grunt is still in his tank, or Thane has not been recruited) then the mission of the next character present will unlock instead. Speaking with Kelly Chambers between missions will let you know which squad members you can talk to for new loyalty missions. Gaining the loyalty of a squad member unlocks their "Bonus Power" for them to use. The first time a Bonus Power is ever unlocked, it is also added to the Advanced Training list for Shepard. Each squad mate also has one Normandy Upgrade or research project to unlock in the research lab. Once Shepard has access to the research lab, these can be unlocked, even during Act 1, by talking to the squad members before they offer their loyalty missions and selecting the "\[NORMANDY UPGRADES]" option under the Investigate heading; otherwise it unlocks automatically as each loyalty mission is complete. Miranda: The Prodigal Jacob: The Gift of Greatness Jack: Subject Zero Mordin: Old Blood Grunt: Rite of Passage Garrus: Eye for an Eye Samara: The Ardat\-Yakshi Tali: Treason Thane: Sins of the Father Legion: A House Divided

The following DLC becomes available for the first time when Act 2 begins. These are both large, substantial, and challenging undertakings, and offer significant rewards. Lair of the Shadow Broker Arrival

Several key progression missions take place during the course of Act 2\. Only the Reaper IFF mission may be done whenever you're ready; the other two trigger automatically. Collector Ship \- triggered a few missions after the events on Horizon. See the acquisition section on the mission page for specifics. Reaper IFF \- choose anytime after the Collector Ship mission. **However**, once completed, a mission countdown activates, with the possibility of significant plot consequences if the player delays much before proceeding through the Omega 4 Relay and beginning Act 3\. Await IFF Installation \- triggers aboard the Normandy immediately after obtaining the IFF from the Derelict Reaper.

Act 3, also known as the Suicide Mission, begins when the Normandy enters the Omega 4 Relay, which can be done freely any time after Await IFF Installation is complete. At this point the mission sequence is locked, and the game proceeds through to the Epilogue without any intervening break for Shepard to use the Galaxy Map, complete assignments, research upgrades, etc. If Shepard survives the Suicide Mission, however, additional missions and assignments (DLC or left over from Acts 1 and 2\) can then be completed. Before entering the Omega 4 Relay and thus launching Act 3, you will want to upgrade your ship. The important upgrades are the shields, the armor, and the cannon. Tali, Jacob, and Garrus, respectively, provide these upgrades. For each of these you do not upgrade, you will later lose one team member. Upgrades will also increase the Normandy's value as a War Asset in Mass Effect 3. The following list shows, in order of preference, which crew member will die if you haven't upgraded a particular part: - **Heavy Ship Armor**: Jack - **Multicore Shielding**: Kasumi, Legion, Tali, Thane, Garrus, Zaeed, Grunt - **Thanix Cannon**: Thane, Garrus, Zaeed, Grunt, Jack, Samara/Morinth **Note:**  This tier is sorted by the characters' order of dying in descending order. Squad members on the "Multicore Shielding" list will not die if they are in your party when you fight the Oculus. Bringing Jack to fight the Oculus will not protect her if you do not have Heavy Ship Armor, nor will bringing anyone on the "Thanix Cannon" list save them from their fate.

The Normandy Attacked \- Defend the Normandy from the Oculus. Collector Base: Infiltration \- Help your tech specialist through the ventilation shaft. Collector Base: The Long Walk \- Your biotic specialist escorts you through the Seeker Swarms. Collector Base: Final Battle \- Face the truth behind the abductions and make your decisions.

> “ > Jack Wall's score for Mass Effect 2 perfectly blends classic sci\-fi inspired sounds with unique arrangements to achieve an emotionally charged complement to the dramatic, action\-packed gameplay. — Dr. Ray Muzyka, BioWare Co\-Founder Mass Effect 2 Original Videogame Score was released on January 18, 2010 and is the main soundtrack for the Mass Effect 2 video game. Jack Wall, as lead composer of his audio production team "Wall of Sound", is credited for the composition and production of the Mass Effect 2 score. Team members included Sam Hulick, David Kates, Jimmy Hinson; and additional music, editing, and implementation was made by Brian DiDomenico. Wall, Hulick and Kates returned to work on the Mass Effect 2 video game score after having also worked on the original Mass Effect video game score, and ultimately the first Mass Effect Soundtrack. In May 2021, BioWare released this soundtrack in a free bonus content download, also featuring items from Deluxe versions of Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3. It is only available until July 31, 2021 or until download limit is reached. The PlayStation 3 version of Mass Effect 2 was developed by BioWare and published by Electronic Arts. The PlayStation 3 version uses a variation of the game engine being developed for Mass Effect 3. The game was released on January 18, 2011 in North and South America, on January 21, 2011 in Europe, and January 27 in Australia and New Zealand. The full version of the game is also available for download through the PlayStation Network.

Copies of the PlayStation 3 version of Mass Effect 2 include the following: - The full Mass Effect 2 game - Blood Dragon Armor - Kasumi \- Stolen Memory - Overlord - Lair of the Shadow Broker - One Cerberus Network activation code.

All other downloadable content for Mass Effect 2 was made available for PlayStation 3 owners to purchase. In addition, several "exclusive" free and paid DLC packs were released. These DLC packs contain Mass Effect 2 content that Xbox 360 and PC owners already have or had access to, but which PS3 owners are unable to obtain otherwise. These packs include: - Terminus Weapon and Armor - Recon Operations Pack - N7 Complete Arsenal Bundle Since the original Mass Effect was not initially available on the PlayStation 3, Mass Effect: Genesis, a brief "interactive comic" which gives players the back\-story of the Mass Effect universe and allow them to make choices which will affect their playthroughs of Mass Effect 2, was made available for download as part of the Cerberus Network.

Following the release of the PlayStation 3 version of Mass Effect 2, numerous players reported that their save files were being corrupted. This corruption forced a console restart and rendered all Mass Effect 2 save files unplayable. While a patch to resolve the issue was pending approval by Sony, BioWare's Chris Priestly suggested that players could avoid the save file corruption by shutting down and restarting the game every few hours, before the corruption had a chance to occur. The patch was released on February 21, 2011 and the save file corruption problem was repaired.

*Main article: Mass Effect 2 Guide* In Mass Effect 2, it is possible for Commander Shepard and members of the team to die at the conclusion of the game's final mission. Throughout the game the player will be building up the team, resources, information and ship necessary to succeed in the final mission. Should the player enter the final mission unprepared it is possible to experience an ending where Shepard dies, members of the team die, or even a disastrous ending in which everyone dies. If Shepard dies, the player will be unable to continue playing the game after the credits, and will be unable to import their character into Mass Effect 3. Death is final for all characters, and any who die during the ending will not appear in Mass Effect 3\.
